source: Navin's brief for Task 046, 26 October 2026: eleven visual grammar rules added to the twelve of the epithelium benchmark (benchmarks/epithelium_animation.json, B-01 to B-12), and the wording rule W-01. The director reads the rules; the checks enforce what code can check (bie/brain/shots.py).
numbering: Navin's brief numbers the grammar rules G-01 to G-11. In this rulebook they are VG-01 to VG-11, because G-01 to G-07 are already the general rules of vision-2026-10-21.json and a rule id is used once.
notes: Each rule is an instruction for the director and the visual section (rule) and a yes/no question for the reviewer (check). Rules change only through a reviewed version bump; Navin approves every new or changed rule.
changes: 2026-10-26.2 (Navin, 26 October 2026): VG-01 names the pace as a visual-change rate with its two bands; the per-video '90 % of shot seconds at L3 or above' check is withdrawn (visual_levels.json, targets).

rules.rule: One topic, one 3D world: the camera moves to the next part; cuts are rare. The pace is the visual-change rate (a block or camera change, or the lit structure moving): micro biology every 3-5 seconds, as the benchmark; engineering and physics worlds every 10-20 seconds (Navin, 26 October 2026).
rules.check: Does the video stay in one world, moving the camera between parts with few cuts, and does the picture change at its subject's pace (micro 3-5 s, engineering and physics 10-20 s)?

rules.rule: Labels are code text tied to their object by a leader line and move with it; a label is never baked into an image, so one asset works in every language.
rules.check: Is every label code text with a leader line to its object, none drawn inside a picture?

rules.rule: Inside is shown by opening or cutting: an exploded view or a cutaway, never a separate flat picture of the inside.
rules.check: When the sentence is about the inside of a thing, does the shot open or cut it (exploded view, cutaway)?

rules.rule: Size is taught by scale comparison with a thing the learner knows (one book = 1 MB; access time as a distance), never by a number alone.
rules.check: Is every size or quantity shown against a known thing, not only spoken as a number?

rules.rule: Equations build step by step beside the picture they describe, each step appearing on its spoken words.
rules.check: Does every equation build one step at a time, next to its picture, on the words that say that step?

rules.rule: Graphs draw themselves as a lit line; a slope or tangent moves along the curve while it is spoken about.
rules.check: Does every graph draw itself, with a moving slope or tangent where one is spoken about?

rules.rule: Two things are compared on a split screen (the split_compare block), the same slots on both sides.
rules.check: Is every comparison a split screen with the same slots on both sides?

rules.rule: Processes show flow with moving arrows or particles (magma, water, concrete, ions, mucus), never a still diagram with static arrows.
rules.check: Does every process shot move: arrows or particles travelling along the path?

rules.rule: One dark background, one accent colour per concept, one camera language per video.
rules.check: Is the background dark throughout, each concept in its one accent colour, and the camera language the same for the whole video?

rules.rule: History and polity use a lit timeline with nodes; maps appear only through the licence gate's map rule (India's boundary waits for Navin's approval).
rules.check: Do history and polity shots use a lit timeline with nodes, and does every map pass the licence gate's map rule?

rules.rule: A story or guide character appears only where the topic and the level ask for it (young classes, story topics), as a 2D illustrated character; no Pixar-style acting.
rules.check: If a character appears, do the topic and the level ask for one, and is it a 2D illustrated character without Pixar-style acting?

rules.rule: The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE teaches as a teacher: it says the fact itself. Navin accepts the copyright position (26 October 2026).
rules.check: Does any sentence point at the book, its pages, its author or its figures instead of teaching the fact itself?

W-01.decided: Navin, 26 October 2026: narration never says 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says' or any wording that points at the book. BIE teaches as a teacher.
W-01.how: Regular expressions, case-insensitive; Devanagari words are bounded by Devanagari letters, Roman words by Roman letters (bie/brain/soul.py, book_pointing). A sentence that matches any pattern goes back to the maker as a W-01 problem; the lesson's wording patch round rewrites only those beats.
hinglish: chapter (?:ke anusa+r|ke mutabi[kq]|mein? likha|mein? diya|kehta hai|kahta hai)
mixed: book (?:के अनुसार|के मुताबिक|कहती है|बताती है|कहता है|बताता है|की line|की figure|की table|वाली|का हिसाब)
chapter (?:के अनुसार|के मुताबिक|में लिखा|में दिया|कहता है)
allowed_examples: एक book में लगभग 1 MB text होता है (a scale comparison: the book is an everyday thing, not the source).
इस table को देखो: shape → job (the board on screen, not the book's table).
Exam में यह line सीधे पूछी जाती है (the exam, not the book).
पहला figure 4 forms की side और top views देता है (the figure BIE draws on screen: a teacher pointing at the screen, not at the book; Navin may add it to the list).
Panel (a), Squamous, tiles जैसी पतली 1 sheet है (the panel letters are on BIE's own drawing).
refused_examples: किताब के अनुसार epithelium covering बनाता है।
Book में इसे simple squamous कहा गया है।
As the book says, the cells are tightly packed.
NCERT kehta hai ki basement membrane non-cellular hai.
Book short cylindrical कहती है; height और width लगभग बराबर समझो।
book nucleus और cytoplasm के न रहने की बात करती है।
Printed location है ‘The outer or apical layer of the cell’।
